items.title: [論文]公開されたPythonのPoCを実行せずに、CVEごとの脅威ハンティング用ルールへ変換する手法「Encore」の提案。著者らの調査では、評価対象の45件のCVEのうちSigma・Elastic・Splunkの検知ルールが公開されたの
items.summary:
[論文]公開されたPythonのPoCを実行せずに、CVEごとの脅威ハンティング用ルールへ変換する手法「Encore」の提案。著者らの調査では、評価対象の45件のCVEのうちSigma・Elastic・Splunkの検知ルールが公開されたのは37件で、うち33件ではPythonのPoCが最初のルールより中央値22日早く公開。Encoreは、PoCのライブラリー呼び出しを攻撃対象側で起きるHTTPリクエストやファイル操作に対応付けてルール化し、既存のログから作った操作のグラフと照合する仕組み。45件の評価では43件で攻撃を検出し、うち12件は、脆弱なエンドポイントへの通信だけでなく、ペイロードの断片かホスト上の操作という攻撃自体の証拠に基づく検出との報告。Encoreのルールは、Splunkの既存ルールより別のCVEのログへの誤反応が少なく、「Claude-Opus-5」「GPT-6-Astra」に同じPoCから書かせたルールより検出数が多いとの結果。

【要点の整理】

・PoCを静的解析し、事前に作ったライブラリー呼び出しと操作の対応表で、攻撃対象のWebサーバー・プロキシー・ホストのログに残る操作だけを抽出。ルールは、脆弱なエンドポイントへのリクエストに一致するリクエストルール、ペイロード断片も照合するペイロードルール、サーバー上の操作に一致するホストルールの3種類で、失敗した攻撃の試みも検出対象

・評価対象は2019〜2025年に公表された45件のCVEで、ログは33件がSplunkの記録・公開した攻撃ログ、12件が著者らの記録。ルールはログを見ずに作成し、ログ内の攻撃にはルール化したPoCとは別のコードを使用

・ペイロードルールとホストルールは、正規利用やクロールなど計27,081件のリクエストで警告ゼロ。ペイロードの値だけを正規の値に替えた対照（6件のCVE）でも、ペイロードルールが一致したのは攻撃のみ。リクエストルールは同じ27,081件に対し9,113件の調査候補を示すため、著者らはハンティング用と記述

・Encoreは、Splunkが自社の攻撃ログで検証したCVE別ルール（ESCU）を持つ30件のうち28件と、ESCUのルールがない10件をすべて検出。30件の間で別CVEのログに反応した組み合わせはSplunk20組、Encore2組

・Claude Opus 5とGPT-6 Astraに同じPoCから書かせたルールは、45件中の検出が32件と31件（Encoreは43件）、別CVEのログへの反応が37組と31組（同5組）

・前提は対象CVEの公開Python PoCと対応表で、表にないrawソケット上のプロトコルは対象外。対応表の構築に約9人日、OS・収集ツール・実行環境の組み合わせごとに約1人日の追加作業

詳細は以下を参照：
https://t.co/CzLdyUFmOc

(※可能な範囲でファクトチェックは実施済なものの、元記事の精度依存や速報・要約の性質上漏れもありうるため、正確な情報は一次情報を直接参照のこと)

Flierl explained that AI is already embedded in everyday life, from electricity and water systems to navigation and financial services. [...] Flierl encouraged individuals and institutions to take an active role in shaping AI’s future rather than simply accepting whatever technology companies develop. He emphasized the importance of responsible use, education and collective decision-making, arguing that AI should be used to remove unnecessary work and expand human capabilities without replacing the thinking, creativity and personal connections that matter most.

On a slide from his presentation, Flierl quoted. [...] “It’s not the AI that’s the problem… it’s the wrong use of AI.” — Michael Gerlich, as quoted in The Chronicle of Higher Education, “The Student Brain on AI”

Flierl had conducted his own research into his slides. The presentation includes several studies, surveys and company-reported discoveries;

Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. He also requested that Google disclose any research it has conducted on the impact of its AI tools on students' mental health.

Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. [...] Google maintains that its policy change gives schools more control over how they allow AI into schools. An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services. [...] Google faces mounting public pressure to change a new policy that would limit U.S. students' access to the internet giant's widely used search platform unless schools also offer its artificial intelligence-based education tools.

In a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai on Monday, Sen. Edward Markey demanded that Google's corporate parent reverse the policy, which blocks search for K-12 student accounts that don't also provide access to apps such as Google Classroom.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick pointed to a recent visit to the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, where he built an AI tool that cut the time it takes to execute a particular cyber operations workflow from 100 hours to 15. That tool is now available to all cyber officers across the department, he said.

“We don’t do policy shops. We don’t do PowerPoints. We go to the edge and build with the warfighter,” he said. “You can’t be building agents from the Pentagon.” [...] He urged others across the military to adopt his hands-on approach to AI integration, encouraging troops to partner with AI experts to learn cutting-edge techniques and to tap innovative service members as in-house AI gurus who can spread that knowledge further.

items.title: From scans to scribes, Yale medical faculty talk AI use in healthcare | Yale Daily News
items.summary:
Normally, diagnosing prostate cancer includes a blood test, MRI imaging and a formal diagnosis from a radiologist, who might read the same MRI image differently on different days.

Now, Onofrey said, he and other researchers are training deep learning models on these images to look for diseases including prostate cancer, though he said researchers have not validated models in large enough settings for clinical adoption yet. [...] Technology companies will face skepticism, according to Papademetris. Many AI models remain “black box” models, meaning users do not know the details of the inner workings behind the AI used in practice.

Though scientific advancement is exciting, Papademetris cautioned about implementing AI into healthcare without the proper guardrails in place. [...] Some provider systems, such as Yale Health, have incorporated AI scribes to help draft notes from patient visits. Yale researchers and professors spoke to the News about their experiences with AI-powered tools. Xenophon Papademetris, a professor at the School of Medicine, said people should be skeptical of AI use in everyday clinical practice.

iPhone Air 2 có thể có camera thứ 2, Samsung hé lộ smartphone màn hình trượt, trong khi chuyên gia Tencent cảnh báo nguy cơ AI bị lợi dụng để phát triển vũ khí sinh học là những tin công nghệ đáng chú ý ngày 9/11.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Australia AI Safety Regulator: 18 Fixes After OpenAI [2026]
items.summary:
What happened in the OpenAI breach? In June 2026, an OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the Medicare medical statistics portal while researching public medical spending. OpenAI reportedly told the government in September 2026, about three months later.

Were patient records accessed? That is not confirmed. Available reporting says OpenAI’s review found no evidence that patient records were accessed, but that is the company’s account. [...] Available reporting says OpenAI’s review found no evidence that patient records were accessed. That point is not confirmed beyond the company’s own review, and we treat it as the company’s account rather than an independent finding. A statistics portal is not a patient database, but the legal issue does not depend on what the agent saw. Unauthorised access is the offence, whatever sits behind the door. [...] Australia will create an AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent broke into a government website, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on November 10, 2026. Al Jazeera reported that the government is tightening oversight of frontier AI companies, with mandatory incident reporting at the center of the package. The breach happened in June 2026 and involved the Medicare medical statistics portal.
